newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES MKT SLOW, AWAITS NEWS.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES MKT SLOW, AWAITS NEWS.

text.p: Grains futures traders of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) took a wait-and-see attitude on Wednesday that resulted in a meagre turnover, dealers said.
"Everybody is waiting for new information to trade on," said Sandor Ifju of OTP Forex.
He added that players put out limit-up offers and limit-down bids but hardly any contracts changed hands.

December maize accounted for 110 contracts of Wednesday's 164 contracts or 63.9 million forints grains futures turnover. The price of the December maturity rose 390 forints per tonne to end at 19,000 forints.
October and November maize prices rose by 200 and 50 forints to end at 18,100 and 18,350 forints, respectively.
Milling wheat edged up 10 forints for May and August to close at 24,010 and 21,110 forints, respectively.
Snowfalls started on Tuesday and forecast to last until the end of the month would only have a beneficial effect on crops, if any, traders and meteorologists said.
"Much-needed precipitation would more than offset the possible growth delay caused by recent and expected snowfalls," Attila Bussay of the Met Office's agricultural department said.
